title: U.S. House · Colorado's 8th District
area: North Denver suburbs and Weld County, including Thornton, Greeley and Brighton.

context.text: Ballotpedia identified this as a battleground race for the November 3, 2026 general election. Incumbent Gabe Evans (R) defeated Yadira Caraveo (D) 49.0%-48.2% in 2024, in a district that President Trump won by less than 2 points in 2024. Manny Rutinel won the June 30, 2026 Democratic primary over State Rep. Shannon Bird and Evan Munsing (who unofficially withdrew); Rutinel was appointed to the Colorado House of Representatives in 2023 and did not seek re-election there in 2026. As of June 30, 2026, Evans had raised $5.39 million and Rutinel had raised $4.34 million.

summary.text: Gabe Evans is the incumbent U.S. Representative for Colorado's 8th District, elected in 2024 after defeating Democratic incumbent Yadira Caraveo. He is an Army veteran and former Arvada police lieutenant who served one term in the Colorado House of Representatives. In his Ballotpedia survey, he said he is running on crime, the cost of living, and keeping Colorado affordable and safe.

background.text: Born in Aurora, Colorado, and the grandson of Mexican immigrants, according to his official biography and Ballotpedia. Earned a bachelor's degree in government from Patrick Henry College in 2009.

Served in the U.S. Army and Colorado Army National Guard from 2007 to 2019. According to his official biography, he was a UH-60 Black Hawk pilot and company commander stationed at Buckley Air Force Base, completed a combat deployment in support of Operation Enduring Freedom, and reached the rank of captain.
Joined the Arvada Police Department in 2011 and rose to lieutenant, retiring in 2022 to run for public office. He has also worked as a concealed-carry firearms instructor.
Owns and operates a family farm in southern Weld County with his wife, Anne, according to his official biography; they have two sons.

Elected to the Colorado House of Representatives (District 48) in 2022 and served from 2023 to 2025. According to Wikipedia, he focused on criminal justice issues, including bills on time off for National Guard service.

Announced his candidacy for Colorado's 8th District in September 2023, defeated former state Representative Janak Joshi in the Republican primary, and won the November 2024 general election over incumbent Yadira Caraveo, 49.0% to 48.2%.
Serves in Congress on the Energy and Commerce Committee and the Homeland Security Committee, according to Wikipedia; he is a member of the Problem Solvers Caucus.
Ballotpedia lists past affiliations with Destiny Church in Fort Lupton, the National Rifle Association, and Veterans of Foreign Wars.

priorities.text: Campaign website lists four platform pillars: lowering the cost of living by reducing deficit spending and regulation, focusing the military on "warfighting," expanding educational choice for families, and "defending American values."
priorities.quote: Lower the cost of living by reining in deficit spending and the tax-and-regulate policies that are crushing our economy.

positions.summary: Campaign website says educational freedom means families should be able to choose the education that works best for them.

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on Homeland Security (Counterterrorism and Intelligence; Emergency Management and Technology subcommittees) and the House Committee on Energy and Commerce (Commerce, Manufacturing, and Trade; Energy; Environment subcommittees) in the 119th Congress.

candidates.name: Manny Rutinel
candidates.ballotNote: Won the June 30, 2026 Democratic primary over State Rep. Shannon Bird and Evan Munsing (who unofficially withdrew).
candidates.currentRole: Member, Colorado House of Representatives, District 32 (2023-2026)

summary.text: Manny Rutinel is a Democratic candidate for Colorado's 8th District. He is an attorney and former Army Corps of Engineers economist who served in the Colorado House of Representatives from 2023 until resigning in September 2026 to focus on the congressional race. His campaign materials emphasize lowering costs, taking on corruption, and supporting working families.

background.text: According to Wikipedia, born in Los Angeles and raised by a single mother in the Dominican Republic until age six, then in California and Florida. His campaign website says he grew up in a working-class family that relied on food stamps and Medicaid and that he worked at McDonald's through high school.

Earned an associate degree from Pasco-Hernando State College, a bachelor's degree from the University of Florida (2016), a master's degree in applied economics from Johns Hopkins University (2018), and a J.D. from Yale Law School (2022).
Worked as an economist for the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers from 2016 to 2018 and, according to his campaign website, served as a first responder in Puerto Rico after Hurricane Maria.
After law school, worked as an associate attorney at Earthjustice, according to Wikipedia. Since 2021, he has been chief executive officer of Climate Refarm, a nonprofit.

An Adams County Democratic vacancy committee appointed him to the Colorado House of Representatives, District 32, in October 2023 to replace Dafna Michaelson Jenet, who had been selected for a state Senate vacancy. He won the seat in 2024.

Announced his run for Congress on January 27, 2025, and left the state House on September 4, 2026 to focus on the campaign. In his Ballotpedia survey he said he had sponsored over a dozen bills and cosponsored over 400.

priorities.text: In his Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey response, said he is running in part to oppose planned cuts to the Social Security Administration's workforce and field offices.
priorities.quote: Trump, Gabe Evans, and their billionaire donors plan to lay off half the Social Security workforce and shutter field offices, causing delay, disruption, and denial of earned benefits. It's a backdoor cut that inflicts pain on seniors and people with disabilities, and I'm running to stop it.

record.text: Served as a member of the Colorado House of Representatives, District 32, from October 2023 until leaving office on September 4, 2026.

summary.text: David Wood, a retired computer programmer from Westminster, is running as the Libertarian Party candidate for Colorado's 8th Congressional District. In his Ballotpedia survey, he says he is running on a less interventionist foreign policy, free trade, and limits on executive power.

background.text: Wood is a retired computer programmer living in Westminster, Colorado, with his wife, Betsy, according to his Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey.

priorities.text: Reduce U.S. military intervention abroad, including bringing troops home from overseas bases and reducing the military budget.
Stop deportations of what he calls 'peaceful hard-working immigrants' and increase the number of immigration judges to speed due process.
End tariffs and other federal interventions in the economy, and pass a balanced budget amendment.

positions.summary: Opposes current deportation practices and calls for more immigration judges to speed due process for immigrants.
positions.quote: Stop the shameful deporting of peaceful hard-working immigrants and increase the number of immigration judges so immigrants can get timely due process in applying for citizenship.

positions.summary: Opposes tariffs on imported goods, favoring free trade.
positions.quote: We need Free Trade. Imposing tariffs on foreign goods raises the cost of raw materials and manufactured products, shifting those higher expenses onto us, as struggling consumers.
